purpose: Separate Japanese hull recovery from carrier-air/team recovery and quantify the surface-fleet advantage that survives into early March without turning it into automatic offensive capability.

details.Shokaku: operational after 3-Feb battle; only light topside/splinter damage centered
details.Hiryu: flight-deck physical recovery by late Feb; carrier-team combat-readiness gate 1944-02-23..03-02 now passed
details.Soryu: GALVANIC repair/trials and carrier-team gate completed by mid-Feb

established_core.band_method: Derived from pre-3Feb 219 ready on Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu, 66-79 irrecoverable 3-Feb carrier-battle losses, repairable-aircraft return, Soryu restoration, and one month of replacement/training. It is intentionally below later 4/30 four-core 280-300 ready class.
established_core.main_constraint: experienced strike leaders, navigation/observer teams, multi-seat attack crews and four-deck synchronization; airframes are easier to replace than the human system

Taiho.branch_completion: completed in Feb-1944 per branch construction clock
Taiho.combat_credit: No synchronized fleet-strike deck credit on 8 Mar. May perform trials, deck qualification, ferry/local CAP/training tasks under emergency constraints.
Taiho.integration_gate: late-Mar/early-Apr C+/B- remains plausible; full fifth-carrier integrated use is later and depends on 601st-group/deck-team work-up, not hull completion alone
Taiho.historical_sanity_anchor: Historical Taiho commissioned 7 Mar, conducted trials through 19 Mar, embarked a full air group late Mar and reached Lingga 5 Apr. Branch hull completion is earlier, but crew/air-group integration is not automatically advanced by the full construction delta.

second_line.roles: training/ferry/rear CAP/replacement absorption plus limited operational strike; not interchangeable with the four-core fast synchronized strike system
second_line.confidence: LOW_MEDIUM until a dated 8-Mar hull-by-hull air-group ledger is built

battleships.roster_logic: Yamato, Musashi, Nagato, Kongo, Haruna, Hiei, Kirishima, Fuso, Yamashiro, Ise, Hyuga; Mutsu remains lost.
battleships.Pacific_mobile_heavy_fast_core: Yamato/Musashi/Nagato + four Kongo-class are the meaningful Pacific heavy pool; speed/role differs by class.
battleships.western_old_battleship_pool: Fuso/Yamashiro/Ise/Hyuga have been used in Bengal/Andaman rotation; if that theater becomes dormant their routine forward exposure can be reduced, but they do not become fast-carrier escorts.

heavy_cruisers.assessment: materially healthier than historical Solomon attrition path; Tone/Chikuma retained in Mobile Fleet scout/screen pool

fleet_destroyers.March_concentration_guard: No major Feb-Mar destroyer attrition erases the branch advantage, but carrier screens, tanker/convoy protection, local fleets and ASW consume many hulls. A one-operation concentratable pool should be treated as roughly mid-30s to mid-40s unless a fresh allocation audit says otherwise.

surface_fleet.judgment: Japan has unusually strong surface and escort depth for 1944, but fuel, air cover, and information quality—not raw hull count—set offensive reach.

system_assessment.fuel_basing: BINDING; Truk no longer suitable as fleet hub
system_assessment.open_ocean_offensive_balance: UNFAVORABLE against even temporarily compressed TF58 because US aircraft mass, CIC/F6F/AA and eight intact fast battleships remain substantial
